data.one_liner: TextMate-grammar based syntax highlighter for Flutter ported from Shiki.
data.what_it_does: Tokenizes source code with real VS Code TextMate grammars and Shiki themes and renders it as styled TextSpans or through dedicated widgets. Supports ~250 languages and 75 themes, running on a background isolate or Web Worker.
use_when: You need accurate syntax highlighting that matches VS Code colors.
You want to display formatted source code inside Flutter widgets.
You need a TextField controller that highlights syntax as users type.
avoid_when: You are building a full-featured code editor with advanced IDE features beyond syntax-highlighted text input.
You want to avoid bundled language grammars and dynamically fetch everything from remote servers without custom loading.
strengths: Golden-tested token output matching VS Code exactly.
Supports off-main-thread background isolate highlighting to keep UI smooth.
Runs on every platform Flutter supports without mandatory native dependencies.
weaknesses: Web async highlighting requires setting up a browser Web Worker.
Very large files still incur Flutter paragraph layout costs.
data.setup_notes: Pure Dart by default with no native build steps required, though an optional Web Worker can be installed for web async support.
data.minimal_example:
ShikiCodeView(
  code: "void main() => print('Hello');",
  lang: CodeLanguages.dart,
  textStyle: const TextStyle(fontFamily: 'FiraCode', fontSize: 14),
)
